To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the glutamic acid‐decarboxylase antiporter is essential for glutamic acid decaboxylase activity and that expression of gadA, gadB and gadC is controlled by H‐NS, RpoS and environmental factors such as acid shock, salt stress or stationary growth phase.

(i) glutamic acid decarbocylase is required for acid resistance in E. coli; (ii) the expression of the glutamic decarboxylating system is induced by acid stress; (iii) the glutamic decarbocylating system is also required for resistance to other stresses; and (iv) the regulation of glutamic acid‐decarboxylating genes is complex and involves at least two different regulatory factors.

In summary, our research is concerned with

the characterization of a novel stress‐inducible system in E. coli, whose activity is strictly dependent on the expression of two genes, gadA, encoding glutamic acid decarbosylase, and gadC, encoding a putative γ‐aminobutirate antiporter, and on the presence of a proton gradient.

the regulation of the glutamate decarboxylating system in response to stationary phase and stress conditions in E. coli, and provides a new insight into the mechanisms controlling the expression of the glutamic decarboxylated system.
the identification of the regulatory mechanisms that control the transcription of the glutamic‐dependent system and the physiological conditions under which this system is expressed.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
RpoS is the major regulator of the glutamic‐acid‐dependent acid resistance system, and H‐NS is an auxiliary repressor.
H‐NS is a repressor and RpoS is an activator of gad gene expression, but the molecular mechanisms by which these regulators act are not yet clear.
the Gad system is expressed in the stationary phase to counteract acid stress and that this regulation is mediated by H‐NS and/or RpoS.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the glutamic acid‐mediated acid resistance system is induced in response to stationary‐growth conditions and that this induction depends on the alternative sigma factor σ ^{s}.
the gad system is a stationary‐phase‐regulated system, and that its expression is under the direct or indirect control of the alternative sigma factor σS.
the glutamic acid‐decarboxylation system is a major component of the E. coli acid‐resistance mechanism.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the Gad system represents the major glutamic acid‐decarboxylation pathway in E. coli, which is induced by acidic shock and growth‐phase transition, in a manner that is regulated at the transcriptional level by the H‐NS/RpoS regulatory cascade.
the glutamic acid‐based system is a key component of the acid resistance of E. coli, which can be modulated by the growth stage and the environmental conditions.
glutamic acid decarbosylase is the key enzyme for acid resistance in E. coli.
